timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: Azure encrypts everything by default, right? So why worry?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Default encryption uses platform-managed keys. CMK means YOU control the keys. Big difference in compliance and control.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What's the difference between PMK and CMK?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: PMK — Azure manages keys, you get encryption. CMK — you bring your own key from Key Vault. You decide when it rotates or gets revoked.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Two layers of encryption with different algorithms. Even if one is compromised, the other still protects your data.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: TLS 1.2 minimum. Azure enforces it across all services. No more unencrypted traffic between components.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: It encrypts data while it's being processed in CPU memory. Even the cloud provider can't see it.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: It's hardware-level encryption using AMD SEV-SNP. Microsoft, Google, and Oracle all offer it now.
